I farm in Quzhou County, so at the start of the growing season I would keep to the wheat-maize rotation that fits this area best. I would first carry my winter wheat through to harvest, because it is already in the ground, I know how to manage it, and it spreads my risk better than switching into something unfamiliar. After wheat harvest, I would plant summer maize on the same land, because that is the most reliable follow-up crop here with the local climate, my labor, and my schooling level. I would not make the plan too complicated. I would use improved or hybrid seed where it clearly helps yield and stability, but I would keep management simple: moderate fertilizer, several irrigations when the crop really needs water, routine pest control rather than excessive spraying, and conventional tillage that I already know how to do. My goal would be steady output and lower risk, not chasing the highest possible yield with a complicated program.
